At its peak, around the mid-1950s, the gap was roughly 45 to 50 percentage points. In Gallup's 1956 polling, about 14% of Southerners approved of Black and white children attending the same schools, against roughly 60% outside the South. The team note's "nearly the full scale" overstates it, because a large minority outside the South still disapproved and the South wasn't at zero. These figures come from my memory of Gallup trends, so they may be off by a few points.

CONFIDENCE: 55
